prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: porting a mortgage to a new property. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member wants to port a mortgage, I check the sale and purchase timelines together, because the old loan can only move cleanly if the existing property completes and the new one completes within the agreed portability window."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the new property is more expensive than the old one, I treat the extra borrowing as a fresh affordability decision, because porting usually covers only the balance of the existing mortgage and not the full price uplift."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member is keeping the same mortgage product, I still re-check the product rules at the time of application, because some features, fee arrangements or fixed-rate conditions may not carry over exactly as expected."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is any uncertainty about whether the sale will complete first, I ask for a realistic fallback plan, because a failed port can create a temporary need for repayment funds or bridging arrangements."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the new property is of a different type, I reassess the risk from scratch, because moving from a standard house to a flat, a leasehold property or a property with unusual construction can change the underwriting view."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is porting and increasing borrowing, I separate the existing loan from the new advance in the case notes, because the different parts may have different rates, terms and affordability checks."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the new property has a higher value but also higher ongoing costs, I include those costs in the affordability picture, because ground rent, service charges, maintenance and commuting changes can affect the practical monthly budget."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member mentions improvements or incomplete works at the new property, I ask for clarification early, because a port can be delayed if the home is not suitable as security at completion."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the old mortgage has any arrears, payment difficulties or special arrangements, I pause and review carefully, because portability is not automatic and the member’s conduct on the existing account still matters."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a porting case is straightforward, I still keep a tight paper trail of offer dates, valuation dates and completion dates, because the process depends on evidence that both the old and new security positions are properly aligned."}]}
